skill.description: Retrieve Xiaohongshu creator profiles through SocialDataX using an account ID, profile URL, or shared profile text.

security_audit.summary: All 32 static findings concern Markdown, documented authentication, service links, creator identifiers, or readable multilingual text rather than demonstrated threats. A separate supply-chain risk exists because the examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx with automatic installation approval. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection in the two files; external package behavior remains unverified.

remediation.issue: CLI examples automatically execute an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version, verify package provenance and integrity, and request explicit user approval before installing or executing it.

content.value_statement: Creator screening requires consistent profile facts before partnership decisions. This skill guides SocialDataX lookups and separates visible account data from strategic judgments.
actual_capabilities: Guide creator profile lookup using one platform account ID, profile URL, short link, or shared profile text.
Provide direct CLI examples and select corresponding MCP tools when those tools are already available.
Summarize returned profile facts, including nickname, biography, verification, follower counts, and other visible account fields.
Separate reported facts from creator positioning and partnership screening judgments.
Handle lookup errors with one ordinary retry and stop repeated requests after insufficient balance errors.
limitations: Live lookups require SocialDataX access, a configured API key, network access, and sufficient provider balance.
The CLI requires Node.js and npm; the two supplied files contain no executable implementation for independent verification.
Returned fields vary; profile signals do not establish audience quality, purchase intent, or partnership performance.
The documented workflow is read-only and does not log in, publish, like, comment, or modify accounts.

use_cases.title: Screen a Potential Brand Partner
use_cases.description: Review a creator profile and distinguish visible account evidence from assumptions about brand fit.

use_cases.title: Prepare Creator Intake Notes
use_cases.description: Summarize an account ID or profile link into consistent facts and follow-up questions for representation discussions.

use_cases.title: Review Account Positioning
use_cases.description: Inspect your visible biography, verification, and follower signals before deciding which profile details need further review.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize One Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up this Xiaohongshu profile: [profile URL]. Summarize available account facts and mark missing fields as unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Known Creator ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the XHS profile for [user ID]. Report biography, verification, follower count, and visible engagement signals without inferring unavailable demographics.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Preliminary Brand Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [profile share text] for [brand category]. Separate returned profile facts from tentative fit judgments and list evidence needed before outreach.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Creator Shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up each creator separately: [profile links]. Compare available profile fields, distinguish facts from judgments, and flag evidence gaps for [campaign goals].

output_examples.input: Summarize a creator profile whose response includes a biography and follower count but no verification field.
output: Illustrative summary: The returned biography describes skincare reviews, and the account reports 18,000 followers.
Interpretation: The stated topic may fit a skincare campaign, but profile data alone does not establish audience relevance.
Next question: Which recent posts and engagement results should be reviewed before outreach?

output_examples.input: The creator lookup returned an insufficient balance error.
output: The lookup did not return profile data because the provider balance is insufficient.
No repeated request was made. Resume the failed lookup after you confirm that the account balance is available.

best_practices: Use one supported identifier per lookup and reuse known platform IDs when available.
Keep API keys in the configured environment and exclude secret values from prompts, logs, and shared reports.
Review and pin the CLI package before execution; label missing fields and separate profile facts from screening judgments.
anti_patterns: Do not infer audience authenticity, conversion rates, or campaign outcomes from follower counts alone.
Do not combine account ID and profile URL entry points in one request.
Do not repeatedly retry insufficient balance errors or authorize unrelated system changes to repair the environment.

faq.question: Which inputs are supported?
faq.answer: Use a Xiaohongshu account ID, profile URL, short link, or shared profile text. Select one entry point per call.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Configure SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY and provider access. Direct CLI usage also requires Node.js and npm; existing MCP tools provide an alternative entry point.

faq.question: Does the workflow modify my account?
faq.answer: The documentation specifies read-only profile queries without login or account actions. External package behavior was not verified from these files.

faq.question: Are all profile fields guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Available fields depend on the provider response. Missing fields should remain unavailable rather than being inferred.

faq.question: Is provider access free?
faq.answer: The documentation describes account balance requirements and billing recovery. Check current SocialDataX pricing; this skill provides no pricing guarantee.

faq.question: Can this replace a complete partnership evaluation?
faq.answer: No. It supports preliminary profile screening. Review content, audience evidence, engagement quality, and campaign requirements before making partnership decisions.
